topics.topic: Exact event when a folder or file name is observed and fixed for an operation
questions: At which exact event is a folder name observed: directory-entry enumeration, metadata read, file open, or completion of the scan, and must that one observation govern all later checks in the operation?
At which exact event is the name fixed for this scan: directory listing, per-entry metadata read, file open, or another defined instant?
At which exact event is a name considered observed: directory enumeration, metadata read, opening, or another defined step?

quotes: A name is judged when the folder is observed.

A file that
disappears before its metadata is read is not reported.

A
file renamed after the observation is no longer at the observed path, so reading it for placing fails
with `unreadable_file` (A3 rule 4).
judgement.divergence: One implementation fixes the name during directory enumeration and later reports `unreadable_file`; another fixes it during metadata reading and ignores the renamed conflict copy, which the calling flow observes as different scan results.
judgement.why: The phrase “when the folder is observed” does not identify the event that fixes a name, and the choice changes the reported result during a rename race.

witness.observer: The calling flow reading the scan result.

topics.topic: How INV-18 proves the ordinary file, not the identical conflict copy, sourced the placement
questions: What must the INV-18 test show to prove that the conflict copy was not the source of the new placement when the ordinary file has identical content?
How must the test demonstrate that the ordinary file, rather than the ignored conflict copy with identical content, was the source read for the new placement?

quotes: - INV-18: a Syncthing conflict copy is neither reported by a scan nor the source of a new placement.

R0-14 concerns files, not content: a conflict copy is
never a source of a new placement, an ordinary file with the same content as a conflict copy is placed
as usual, and content that already has a placement replays under A3 rule 2 whatever name it has now.
an ordinary file with the content of a conflict copy is placed (`test_an_ordinary_file_is_placed_when_a_conflict_copy_has_the_same_content`)
judgement.divergence: One implementation reads the ordinary file; another searches by hash and reads the ignored conflict copy. If the ordinary path disappears after observation while the conflict copy remains, the calling flow receives failure from the first and a placement from the second.
judgement.why: The Required tests item requires only that the shared content be placed and does not say what must be shown to prove that the ordinary path supplied the bytes.

An implementation that searches by hash reads the ignored conflict copy and creates a placement.
witness.observer: The calling flow receiving the placement outcome.

topics.topic: Whether an existing placement replays instead of renamed-file or conflict-copy failure
questions: Must this failure occur only when the content has no existing placement, or does it also override the rule that placed content replays when only a conflict copy holds it?
Does this renamed-file failure apply when the content already has a placement, or does replay take precedence without reading the renamed file?
When the requested hash already has a placement and only a conflict copy contains that content, must placement replay the stored result or fail with `not_ready_or_absent`?

quotes: content that already has a placement replays under A3 rule 2 whatever name it has now.
Placed content replays when only a conflict copy still holds it (`test_placed_content_replays_when_only_a_conflict_copy_still_holds_it`)

Placing an existing placement answers `replayed` with the stored placement and the current
   `photo_id` of its mark, if any, and writes nothing, even when the source file has left the
   folder.
judgement.why: Existing-placement replay takes precedence regardless of the current name; the conflict-copy and renamed-file failures apply when a new placement would have to read the source.

topics.topic: Clock source used for the current instant in age calculations
questions: Which clock supplies the current instant used to calculate file age during scans and placement checks?

quotes:
The system clock is the one source of the current time, declared as `rules.time_source_policy`
   and reaching code through `system_clock_backend` as the operation `utc_now`.
judgement.why: The clock-source rule is unchanged from the text with which State 2 was closed, and the conflict-copy changes did not make this question newly material.

topics.topic: How often the clock is read during scans or multi-item placement
questions: Does a scan or multi-item placement read the clock once for the entire operation, once per file, or at some other specified points?

quotes:
Scan, placement and mark each read it once, after the token, the request form and the path
   identifiers are accepted and before the project lock is taken or any connection, file or record is
   examined.
judgement.why: The once-per-operation clock rule is unchanged from the closed State 2 text, and the reopening did not affect its frequency.

topics.topic: How placement handles a path that reappears after observation and detects a past rename
questions: What must happen if the observed path exists again at placement time—for example because the file was renamed away and back, or another file with the same content replaced it—and how is a past rename distinguished from an unchanged file?

quotes: A placement is identified by the project and the SHA-256 of the source content (R0-10).

Inside the call the folder is scanned once. A requested source with no placement that this scan
does not report as `ready` fails with `not_ready_or_absent`. A source reported `ready` whose
bytes no longer have the requested hash when it is read for placing fails with `source_changed`.

A replaced source is a new photo. The earlier placement, its stored image and its mark stay.
   Removing a source changes no placement (R0-10).
judgement.why: Placement uses the operation’s scan and source-content hash rather than historical file identity, so a currently ready path containing the requested bytes may be placed without detecting an earlier rename.

quotes:
The current time is a `datetime` in UTC without an offset, with microsecond precision and no
   rounding, written in ISO 8601 form. It decides the settling status and sets `marked_at`.

A request
   refused after it, and a replayed mark, have read it and write nothing.
The same `photo_id` again answers `replayed` with the first mark.

- Continuity: The first mark stands when it is sent again, and its `marked_at` does not change

topics.topic: UTC conversion rules for camera times and use of the timezone setting
questions: How is a camera-record time converted to UTC when it has no offset, has an offset, or falls in an ambiguous or nonexistent local time, and what role does the `timezone` setting play?

quotes:
The photo moment is the first usable value of: EXIF `DateTimeOriginal`, EXIF `DateTime`, then
   the file's modification time. `DateTimeOriginal` uses `OffsetTimeOriginal` when that offset has
   the form `+HH:MM` or `-HH:MM`; otherwise it is read in the configured time zone, and so is
   `DateTime`. A camera value is unusable when it is malformed, when its UTC year
   is before 2000, or when it is more than 24 hours after the file's modification time.

The photo date is delivered as UTC without an offset, as the Client Portal stores it. A camera
   time with no offset is read in the configured time zone. A local time that occurs twice is the
   first occurrence, and a local time that does not exist is read with the offset in force before
   the clock change. A modification time is an absolute instant converted to UTC.
| `timezone` | `str` | `Europe/Madrid` |
judgement.why: The camera-time conversion, ambiguity rules and configured timezone are unchanged from the closed State 2 text, and the reopening did not make them newly material.

questions: Must this test also assert that the failed placement creates no stored binary, placement record, or other write, as required to show that the conflict copy was not the source of a new placement?

a conflict copy in the folder and in a subfolder, each with the mark in lower, upper and mixed case, is absent from the scan and placing it by its hash fails with `not_ready_or_absent` (`test_a_syncthing_conflict_copy_is_neither_offered_nor_placed`).

Placing an existing placement answers `replayed` with the stored placement and the current
   `photo_id` of its mark, if any, and writes nothing, even when the source file has left the
   folder.
judgement.divergence: One test checks only the returned `not_ready_or_absent`; another also checks that no binary, placement record or other durable state was written. An implementation accepted by the first can make a later request replay the hidden placement, which the calling flow notices.
judgement.why: The Required tests item names the failure result but does not require evidence that the failed conflict-copy placement wrote no durable state.

witness.initial: No placement exists for hash H, and only an ignored conflict-copy file contains H.
events: The calling flow requests placement of H.
The implementation writes a stored binary and placement record but returns `not_ready_or_absent`.
The calling flow later requests placement of H again.
outcomes: If the failed call wrote nothing, the later request again fails with `not_ready_or_absent`.
If the failed call secretly wrote a placement, the later request answers `replayed` with that placement.
witness.observer: The calling flow receiving the later placement outcome.
basis:

   `photo_id` of its mark, if any, and writes nothing, even when the source file has left the

topics.topic: Whether an ordinary file can place content when a conflict copy has the same hash
questions: When an ordinary file and a conflict copy have identical content and therefore the same hash, does placement by that hash succeed through the ordinary file or fail because a conflict copy also has the hash?

quotes:
R0-14 concerns files, not content: a conflict copy is
never a source of a new placement, an ordinary file with the same content as a conflict copy is placed
as usual
an ordinary file with the content of a conflict copy is placed (`test_an_ordinary_file_is_placed_when_a_conflict_copy_has_the_same_content`)
judgement.why: The rule expressly says that an ordinary file remains an eligible source even when an ignored conflict copy has identical content, so placement succeeds through the ordinary file.
